text:
mira: Quick Q — integrating the browser SDK into our React app. Where should we stash the client token for streaming? I'm seeing CORS errors on /v1/stream when sending Authorization header.

alex: Don't embed long-lived keys in the client. Use a short-lived session token issued from our backend (we usually do /session_token that exchanges the API key for an ephemeral token ~1h). Are you using fetch-based streaming or a websocket approach?

mira: Using fetch-based stream. Error is: 'Access-Control-Allow-Origin' missing. Our Express proxy calls Redwood hosted API and forwards Authorization. Proxy sets headers but maybe preflight failing.

sam: Make sure your proxy handles OPTIONS and returns the right CORS headers. For streaming you often need: 
- Access-Control-Allow-Origin: <origin>
- Access-Control-Allow-Headers: Authorization, Content-Type
- Access-Control-Allow-Methods: GET, POST, OPTIONS
- Access-Control-Expose-Headers: Transfer-Encoding, Content-Length
Also set Access-Control-Allow-Credentials if you're sending cookies.

jordan: Also note: when using fetch streaming + NDJSON, some browsers require exposing certain headers to read them. We typically parse response.body as a ReadableStream and parse chunks.

mira: Server exchange + client snippet I'm using:
```
# server POST /session_token 
body: { scope: "inference:stream" }
# returns { token: "ey..." }

// client
const res = await fetch('/v1/stream', {
  method: 'POST',
  headers: {
    Authorization: `Bearer ${token}`,
    'Content-Type': 'application/json'
  },
  body: JSON.stringify({ prompt })
});
const reader = res.body.getReader();
```

li: For React Native, fetch streaming is flaky. RN's fetch doesn't stream by default on older RN versions. Recommend using a websocket or the RN native module we have in the SDK (we're tracking a small wrapper). For Swift/Kotlin wrappers, use websocket clients or URLSession with StreamTask on iOS to handle incremental data reliably.

alex: Important: Redwood hosted API expects Origin header on browser requests. If your proxy is same-origin (server-side) you can avoid CORS by calling Redwood from server and then proxying processed output to client. If you want direct client->hosted calls, your proxy must forward Origin and the hosted API must see it. Also ensure preflight includes Authorization in Access-Control-Allow-Headers.

mira: One more: retries — if streaming fails halfway through, do we restart or can we resume?

sam: Current recommendation: simple restart with the same prompt; include a resume param if you can track last confirmed token index. We add per-chunk ids in the stream so clients can detect duplicates. We're planning a small helper in the SDK for stream-resume.

alex: I'll draft a short doc snippet for the devex guide and add a code example for the server-side session_token flow + proxy CORS config. I'll ping @mira when it's up.

mira: Awesome, thanks everyone :thumbsup: marking this resolved for now.
